TEN-1.title: Tenant comes from the credential only
TEN-1.mechanism: `TenantScopeMiddleware` reads `tenant_id` from the JWT only; `EndpointSpineTests` bans tenant route and query parameter names by whole-string case-insensitive equality, and bans DECLARED tenant/PII headers via the framework's own `IFromHeaderMetadata` with vendor-prefix and separator normalization; `HostSecurityTests` proves at run time that a forged tenant header in five spellings does not move a request into another tenant; `ContractShapeTests` bans `TenantId` on requests
TEN-1.note: TEN-1 names four surfaces and this edition now reaches all four, unevenly. ROUTE is total, because the pattern loop reads parameter names without consulting a type. HEADER is covered from both sides as of 2026-07-26 (A-2): a declared binding is a scan violation, and a header arriving undeclared is proven not to influence tenant resolution, which is the half no scan can reach. QUERY remains type-dependent: parameter enumeration filters on `BindsFromUrl`, a hand-written enumeration of types, so an `IParsable` value object or a `TimeSpan` binds from the query string and yields nothing to the scan (E-2, not repaired: one predicate cannot serve SEC-2 and SEC-3/TEN-1 at once). Matching is equality against a registry, so a novel spelling walks past (E-9). Findings: A-2 (repaired), E-2 (open), E-9. **Lowered from `proven` to `owed` by the adjudication pass of 2026-07-26 (rulings 5 and 6), through ruling 3's per-obligation structure.** Ruling 5 predicted the header surface would be the falsifying half; it is not, because the flow-back pass built the header mechanism after that section of the digest was drafted, and it reads `proven` above. What falsifies the row is the query enumeration (E-2) and the comparison (E-9), both measured before the ruling and both left open by name.

obligations.name: the tenant is resolved solely from the validated credential
obligations.text: `TenantScopeMiddleware` reads `tenant_id` from the token and from nothing else, which is the half of this claim the second edition cannot reach at all because it can mint no credential.

obligations.name: the route surface is enumerated completely
obligations.text: the pattern loop reads parameter names without consulting a type, so no route parameter is invisible to it; what the predicate then does with the name is the comparison obligation below.

obligations.name: the query surface is enumerated completely
obligations.text: parameter enumeration filters on `BindsFromUrl`, a hand-written list of types, so a value object implementing the framework's parse interface, or a `TimeSpan`, binds from the query string and yields nothing to the scan (E-2) (trigger: the next edition build pass).

obligations.name: the header surface has a mechanism of its own
obligations.text: a header surface cannot be enumerated, so this is the non-scan mechanism ruling 5 requires, and it is covered from both sides as of 2026-07-26: a DECLARED header binding is a scan violation through the framework's own `IFromHeaderMetadata`, with vendor-prefix and separator normalization, and a header arriving UNDECLARED is proven at run time not to move a request into another tenant, in five spellings (A-2).

obligations.name: the request-contract surface is enumerated completely
obligations.text: the contract half rests on `ContractShapeTests`, which is flat and enumerates only `*Request`-suffixed types, so a tenant id nested inside a posted object, or carried by a type whose name it does not recognize, is not reached (E-6) (trigger: MOD-2's delta pass).

obligations.name: the comparison resolves compounds, concatenations and decompositions of a listed word
obligations.text: matching is whole-string case-insensitive equality against a registry; the flow-back pass widened that registry with `workspace` and `account` and their compounds, which is a longer list and not a comparison (E-9) (trigger: the next edition build pass).

SEC-1.title: Every endpoint gated
SEC-1.mechanism: deny-by-default fallback policy (a deny, not `RequireAuthenticatedUser`, so a metadata-free endpoint is unreachable rather than open to every authenticated caller) + cached `PermissionPolicyProvider`; `EndpointSpineTests` resolves the fallback from `IAuthorizationPolicyProvider`, which is what the middleware consults, and EVALUATES it against an anonymous principal and a fully-permissioned authenticated one; it also allowlists `/health` and requires a permission policy per endpoint; the `sv`/tenant gates run after routing and exempt allowlisted-anonymous endpoints
SEC-1.note: The anonymous allowlist is a `(Method, Pattern, Why)` record array as of 2026-07-26 (E-8): keyed on method AND pattern so an anonymous GET no longer pre-authorizes a POST on the same URL, carrying a mandatory justification, matched case-insensitively, and failing on an entry that matches no endpoint. All four proven red separately. The fallback applies to unmatched URLs too, so an unknown route answers 403 rather than 404. The HUM-1 half of E-8 stays open: there is nowhere to declare this surface such that the shared tool VERIFIES an owner exists, which is an adjudication ruling. Findings: E-7 (repaired), E-8 (SEC-1 half repaired, HUM-1 half open).

SEC-2.title: Anti mass-assignment
SEC-2.mechanism: `ContractShapeTests` forbidden-field registry over the Contracts assembly, filtered to types whose name ends in `Request` (FLAT); `EndpointSpineTests` walks every body-bound DTO RECURSIVELY, through public properties, constructor parameters, arrays and generic arguments, with cycle protection and no depth cap, against the same registry; App/Api declare no request/response types
SEC-2.note: The two guards are no longer equivalent and the difference is the point. The HOST scan recurses as of 2026-07-26 (E-6), so a server-controlled field at any depth of any body-bound type on a real route is caught, proven both ways against a nested `AuthorDto` carrying `CreatedBy`. `ContractShapeTests` is STILL FLAT and still enumerates only `*Request` types, so as a second net it reaches one level; repairing it belongs to MOD-2, which has not had its delta pass. A reader taking `proven` to mean both guards reach every depth would be wrong. `IsBodyDto` also excludes types with a null namespace, so a public DTO declared in `Program.cs` is skipped by the host scan entirely (E-6), and `BindsFromUrl` over-excludes the body set (E-2). Findings: E-2 (open), E-6 (host half repaired, contracts half blocked on MOD-2). **Lowered from `proven` to `owed` by the adjudication pass of 2026-07-26 (rulings 2 and 6), through ruling 3's per-obligation structure rather than by collapsing to one word.** No mechanism named above changed and nothing new was discovered: the guards are exactly as measured, and what changed is that the claim now states a completeness obligation and a comparison obligation, and this edition meets neither. The recursive host scan is a real half and reads `proven` above.

obligations.name: the predicate rejects a registry member at any depth of an enumerated type
obligations.text: `EndpointSpineTests` walks every body-bound DTO recursively through public properties, constructor parameters, arrays and generic arguments, with cycle protection and no depth cap, proven both ways against a nested `AuthorDto` carrying `CreatedBy` (E-6).

obligations.name: the enumeration reaches every body-bound type
obligations.text: `IsBodyDto` excludes types with a null namespace, so a public DTO declared in the entry-point file is outside the host scan, and `BindsFromUrl` over-excludes the body set (E-2, E-6). The second net, `ContractShapeTests`, is flat and enumerates only `*Request`-suffixed types, so it reaches one level of the types whose name it recognizes (trigger: MOD-2's delta pass, which owns the placement rule that flat net rests on).

obligations.name: the comparison resolves compounds, concatenations and decompositions of a listed word
obligations.text: matching is a lowercased hash-set lookup, which is equality: a registry entry `status` does not cover `noteStatus`, and widening the list with more spellings is enumeration standing in for a comparison (E-9) (trigger: the next edition build pass, where E-2's split of the one predicate now serving SEC-2 and SEC-3/TEN-1 is the same work).

The sibling edition's SEC-3 survives because it built the three morphological classes explicitly, which is the asymmetry the evidence says exists.

SEC-5.title: No secrets in config
SEC-5.mechanism: `UserSecretsId` + `SecretConfigShapeTests` over every committed JSON config under `src/`, matching secret-shaped keys by TOKEN (camel/Pascal/snake/kebab split) rather than by containment, with a `[Theory]` asserting the predicate's extent + `tools/secret-scan.mjs`, a composed shared-tier scan over every tracked text surface with a `--self-test` mode CI runs before the scan
SEC-5.note: Both mechanisms were blind to the edition's own `Jwt:Key` until 2026-07-26 and both are repaired (E-11). The arch test matched `leafKey.Contains(term)`, which could never fire on a leaf shorter than the term describing it; the CI half was a grep in YAML that was additionally blind to every QUOTED key, meaning every key in every JSON file in the edition (E-16). Four justified exceptions are declared in `secret-scan.allow.json`, each a (file, key) pair with a written reason and a staleness check; one of them is a committed test signing key the repaired scan found on its first run (E-17). Token matching costs a false positive on `TokenCount`, asserted as a passing case rather than hidden (E-9). Still open: `.env` lives inside the repository tree while the claim's statement says development secrets live outside it (E-12), which the scan's tracked-file reading does NOT address. Vault-port interface owed (trigger: first runtime credential).
